speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: Welcome to this ordinary meeting of Hunters Hill Council, number 4483 on this August 10, 2020. I'd like to acknowledge the traditional custodians of the land on which we meet and the waters that surround us, and I pay my respect to elders past and present. Councillor JOHNSTON. Thank you, LORD MAYOR, for the honour of being called by our fellow citizens to this office of honour and trust. Give us grace diligently and honorably, free from private interest or prejudice, to discharge the duties entrusted to us, to the common good, as those in your sight, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. Thank you. Are there any apologies this evening? No apologies? Are there any declarations of interest, please, Councillors? Councillor MILES and Councillor COLLINS. Councillor MILES.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: I refer to 7.2 in the minutes, which is a question that I raised in relation to dangerous drain grates in the Hunters Hill, and I just note the answer is from Council, but I thought that might be from staff, but anyway, I'm just wondering what the insurance implications are for Council if it's aware of the problem and it's an easy fix. What are the insurance implications if we just put it into a long process of rectification? Because I suspect these grates have been placed incorrectly or wrong orientation following the asset management process and also the stormwater management flood management programme that was run when they lifted most of the grates and put cameras and whatever down. So, just wondering where we're situated if we've got this problem and it's not addressed quickly, and it is of major danger to a growing population of bike riders. Where do we stand from an insurance perspective?

speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: Thank you, Councillor. I'll refer this to the General Manager. Councillor JOHNSTON. In response to the specific question, the Works Team inspectors, they matter, of course, when they're out on the job and where there are specific locations where there is an issue, it's helpful to know the location and once, if there is an issue with a particular location, if that can be reported through the customer request system. In relation to your question in insurance, I might ask the Acting Director of Corporate Services to respond to that.

speaker: barryhusking

I've got a mover for that, Councillor CRASSOY. Do I have a seconder? Councillor McLACHLAN. The recommendations there on page one. Councillor CRASSOY.

speaker: elizabethkrassoi
text: Thanks, Mr. Mayor. So, sustainability, by definition, is our capacity to meet our own needs without compromising the ability of future generations to be able to meet their needs as well. So, that falls into three categories. You've got the social aspect, the people. You have the environment, the planet, and you have economic, which is profit. So, sustainability covers all of those things and so it's really great to see the General Manager, Senior Staff, our new Sustainability Officer seeking to engage with our community on that. We have some real talent in our community. So, I'd like to thank the residents who have put their hats in the ring to participate in this three working groups to help Council set some strategies for the future on that. I would like to offer my own services to the committee if I could and I would also hopefully invite Councillor McLACHLAN to ask her if she would participate on the committee as well.

text: Thank you, Councillor CRASSOY.

Because this is a strategy or a policy-based approach, I just believe that that should be amended, that it come back to Council for consideration rather than it just go straight through to Council staff to implement. I think it's important that Councillors be aware of it. So the amendment would be that the matter be brought back to Council once the working parties concluded to assess the priorities.

And there's been more small than big so far, but they've been done with heart and enthusiasm and really well received in the community. It's a really important time for us to just do some good things together. So congratulations to them for putting the effort into it. I think it's resonated well from what I hear. It's also good to have some plans in place for the year ahead. Fingers crossed. And for council, again, to be partnering with events in the community and community groups to collaborate and make good stuff happen as well with council support and with again, their talent and expertise. Old favourites like the Food and Wine Festival will hopefully go ahead next year. And a few new things. And there's some really exciting stuff in the report. Particularly, I'm looking forward to the Henley Farmers Market coming up on the 21st. That's very exciting. I love what they're doing down at Henley Bowling Club. So that should be a great day. And of course, Merton's Faces of Hunters Hill is coming up as well. So yeah, good on the team for making stuff that makes people feel good and feel united as a community happen. We do have an events committee. It's an enthusiastic and talented committee of people. And like all our committees and working groups in Hunters Hill, the people that offer their time and talent to these things do so with generosity and because they believe they have something to offer. So I would hope that in the coming year, we can engage with them some more because what they do, apart from bringing their time and talent and ideas and enthusiasm, is they actually provide a conduit into the community as well. Through their volunteering, usually with more than one group in the community, they tap into their networks. And that is how so many of our events have been made successful and so well-supported by the community in the past. So I would like to...

speaker: clrirmarkbennett
text: Thank you, Councillor CASSIDY. Anybody wishing to speak against? Anybody else for? I'd like to speak for it, if I can. Particularly the staff's response this year to what's happened. We've had a really rough year when you think back to what happened with the storms we had earlier in the year and the way the staff handled those storms was amazing with the help of the SES, followed up by COVID and the need for us to move off site and split up the works teams into pairs so that we could get the work done in a safer way. The way they've responded with PPE and work method statements that keep our people safe, which is really important. No staff, no council meetings. No staff, no action in the community. We've had to keep our people safe and I thank councillors too for their perseverance and not being in our normal position and some of the difficulties of not meeting together. The staff have been going through something which has been quite difficult being away, lots of meetings. I've seen a lot of staff working over weekends and working late into the night trying to organise things and respond to emails only out of necessity really not because they want a word of a night I'm sure. So I'd like to take this opportunity to acknowledge the staff, the great work they've done as a result in particular of the COVID-19 pandemic that we're in and I think if we think that it's gone away we only have to look over our border to the south and realise that the situation could become quite dire very quickly. The mayoral column this week if I might deals just with the pandemic and I'd ask you to share that with as many people as you can. It's still a major issue and I again thank the staff for their great work they've done this year. Thank you. I'll put the motion, the recommendation. Those in favour? Against? That's unanimous. text: I actually don't think it is self-explanatory. We've got a term deposit launched on the 21st of May at 0.66% and four days later at 0.92%. That's a one-third difference. Now I don't think interest rates changed between those times and it's just it doesn't the advice we're getting is not and I don't pretend to be an expert here I don't do much work with fixed interest securities and I wouldn't expect anyone inside council to to have the level the level of expertise to manage $20 million in fixed interest securities. It's a very advanced and very technical area so I'd like to see and I don't know I don't think this requires an amendment or anything like that but I'd like to see somebody come and brief council on on this council laws sometime soon somebody that that's an expert in this field. So basically the three months in the three months that we've had $6 million at 0.01% you know we've probably lost $15,000 okay so it adds up this needs to be done right and and yeah I'm not sure how whether I'm seeing this as a question without notice but I will work with the general manager as I have raised this before but I have been raising this for a couple of years.
